Autoliv's primary goal is to Save More Lives. Our products never get a second chance. This is why we can never compromise on quality. We are working to increase vehicle safety by developing seatbelts, airbags and steering wheels and you can be part of our team as  Cyber Security Architect.
         Should you be interested in overseeing these tasks and aiming for enhanced performance standards, your role will involve:
Own the security architecture for technologies across the IT & Digital domain, ensuring security capabilities work effectively together and integrate seamlessly with the broader enterprise technology landscape.
Define and evolve security architecture principles, reference architectures, standards, and reusable patterns that guide solution architects, domain architects, engineering teams, and security teams.
Embed security by design by partnering with Infrastructure, Solution Owners, and Domain Architects to ensure security requirements and risk considerations are addressed from the earliest stages of solution design.
Assess security risks for new and evolving solutions against Autoliv’s threat landscape and risk appetite, providing clear architectural recommendations and appropriate risk-based controls.
Provide security architecture governance and technical guidance through architectural review boards, ensuring proposed solutions align with security standards, strategic direction, and enterprise architecture principles.
Shape the future security technology landscape by evaluating emerging threats, industry trends, and new technologies, and translating them into actionable architecture roadmaps and target-state designs.
Lead the architectural evaluation and selection of security technologies, including the introduction, modernization, integration, and replacement of capabilities across the security technology portfolio.
Partner with lead engineers from design through initial implementation, translating architecture into practical technical designs while ensuring major changes and new capabilities remain aligned with the approved architecture.
Provide technical leadership across security solutions, steering architectural direction and ensuring consistency across technologies without taking ownership of day-to-day engineering or operational activities.
Contribute to Autoliv’s security strategy and roadmap, working closely with Security Architecture leadership and key stakeholders to align security architecture with business priorities, technology evolution, and the changing threat landscape.
 And If You Have/ Are
 Functional Competencies
Security Architecture & Design: Strong knowledge of security architecture principles, security service design, reference architectures, architectural documentation and modelling, including Enterprise Architecture frameworks such as TOGAF/ADM.
Security Technologies & Platforms: Broad knowledge of on-premises and cloud security technologies, including firewalls, EDR/XDR, WAF, IDS/IPS, DLP, SIEM/SOAR, antimalware and application/network security controls.
Identity, Infrastructure & Cloud Security: Strong understanding of security across enterprise infrastructure and cloud environments, including AD/Entra ID, IAM/PAM, MFA, secrets and credential management, network segmentation, VPN/ZTNA, Zero Trust, DNS security, hardening, vulnerability and patch management.
Cybersecurity Risk & Threat Assessment: Ability to assess architecture and solutions against the threat landscape, identify security risks and translate organizational risk appetite into appropriate architectural requirements and controls.
Security Technology Strategy & Roadmapping: Ability to evaluate security technologies, identify capability gaps, define target-state architectures and develop technology roadmaps considering security effectiveness, integration, scalability and lifecycle.
Security Standards & Architecture Governance: Strong knowledge of security frameworks and standards such as NIST CSF, ISO/IEC 27001 and CIS Controls, with the ability to apply them through architecture reviews, security principles, standards and design decisions.
